options.swap: Whole spices crushed fresh for the pot
options.ratio: 2 tsp blended powder → roughly 1 tbsp whole spices, crushed coarsely just before cooking. For rasam specifically: black peppercorns with a little long pepper (pippali).
options.taste_and_texture: Sharper and more aromatic, and it fades faster, which is why the blend won. Crushing to order is the whole difference and there is no way around the five minutes it costs.
options.nutritional_rationale: Volatile aromatic compounds degrade with time and grinding heat. This is a flavour swap; do not oversell it as a nutritional one.

options.ratio: Replace a quarter of the black pepper by weight with long pepper.
options.taste_and_texture: Sweeter, more resinous heat that sits at the back of the throat. Long pepper is the ingredient most completely lost from South Indian cooking, not merely less common.
options.nutritional_rationale: A flavour restoration, not a nutritional one. Said plainly.

where_it_went: Commercial spice blending produced a consistent, shelf-stable powder cheaper than grinding at home, and the stone went out of the kitchen with it.
